title: Communications
description: Three-tier in-world communication: a proximity speech bubble, an in-world device addressed by player identity (works across spaces), and room broadcast. Adds to — never replaces — the existing room chat.
boundary: Nothing here is wired into engine core. The DM envelope, inbox store, and bubble/phone views are proposed — each only lands in engine/ when a SECOND, unrelated world needs it. Until then this manifest names the boundary so comms-shaped logic never leaks into the kernel.

components.name: Device
components.why: An in-world mobile device on an actor or prop: an identity-addressed phone whose screen shows the active message line. Talk to a person, not a room.
reusableBy: a city-sim with in-world messaging between citizens
a multiplayer life-sim where players ping each other across districts

components.name: Bubble
components.why: A spatial, proximity-gated speech bubble floating over a head — here-and-now talk that fades out, never a log.
reusableBy: a party game with positional voice-lines
an RPG where NPCs speak ambiently as you approach

types.name: DeviceHolder
types.why: A non-player carrier of a device + bubble: NPCs, kiosks, artifacts that can receive a DM or speak spatially.
reusableBy: a quest-giver kiosk in any multiplayer world

behaviors.name: dmEnvelope
behaviors.why: A peer-addressed {t:'dm', to, from, message} message, session.sendDm, and a per-peer dmInbox store. In-room DMs need no transport change; cross-space needs relay identity routing.
reusableBy: any multiplayer game with cross-space direct messages
a collaborative world with private notes between players

behaviors.name: bubbleView
behaviors.why: Screen-space DOM overlay above an entity's head (PeerSelectionLabelProjector pattern), gated on Bubble.speaking and fading on Bubble.since.
reusableBy: a spectator mode with live callouts

behaviors.name: phoneView
behaviors.why: In-world phone mesh with a canvas-texture face showing Device.screen.
reusableBy: a game where gadgets render text in-world
